terms.label: Legal · 01
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of zerosoft.ai and the zerosoft cloud. They are written to be read, not to scare you. We review them periodically and whenever the product changes in a way that affects them. If anything is unclear, write to hola@zerosoft.ai before accepting.

p: The core software is open source (AGPLv3): you can use it, host it and modify it. Enterprise features in the /ee folder are source-available and need a subscription in production. If you use our cloud, you start on a free plan; usage-based pricing will be published before we charge anyone anything, and today nothing is charged.

Do not use any of it to break the law, deceive people or hurt them. Short links in particular are not a tool for phishing or spam, and we will disable links and accounts that do that. The rest of this page is the same idea in more detail.

s02.h: Who we are and what these terms cover
p: zerosoft ("zerosoft", "we", "us") operates zerosoft.ai and the hosted versions of our products: Link (short links, custom domains, link-in-bio pages, QR codes), Cal (scheduling and booking pages), CRM, Track, Chat (a website chat widget) and Docs. Some products or features may be labeled beta; they work, but they can change faster and have rougher edges.

These terms apply to the website and to the hosted service ("the cloud"). If you self-host the software, these terms do not apply to your instance: the software license does. By creating an account or using the cloud you accept these terms and our Privacy Policy. If you accept on behalf of a company or organization, you confirm you are authorized to bind it, and "you" includes it.

zerosoft is open core. All code outside the /ee directory is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPLv3). Code inside /ee is licensed under the zerosoft Enterprise License: free for development and testing, with a subscription required for production use. The license file in each part of the code is the authoritative text.

Your rights to download, run, modify and redistribute the software come from those licenses, not from these terms, and these terms do not restrict them. Conversely, the licenses do not give you any rights over our hosted service, our domains, or the zerosoft name and logo. You may say your project is based on zerosoft, but please do not present a fork or a hosted copy as the official zerosoft service.

If you create an account, we run the software for you. The cloud includes a free plan with usage limits. Beyond those limits it will be billed by usage (for example clicks, bookings, emails, storage or seats), plus taxes where applicable.

Today we do not charge anyone, and we do not collect payment details. Before we charge for anything, we will publish prices on a pricing page and give existing account holders at least 30 days' notice by email. Nothing you do on the free plan will turn into a charge without you first choosing a paid option.
We may change free-plan limits or features. When a change reduces what you already use, we will give reasonable advance notice so you can adjust or export your data.

You sign in with your Google account. We never see or store your Google password. You must be at least 18 years old, or the age of majority where you live, to create an account. Give us accurate information and keep it up to date.

You are responsible for activity under your account and in the workspaces you administer, and for keeping your API keys, webhook secrets and integrations secure. If you suspect unauthorized access, revoke the affected keys and write to security@zerosoft.ai.

Workspace owners and administrators control who joins a workspace and what happens to its content. If you join someone else's workspace, the content you create there belongs to that workspace. Automated access is welcome through the public API, within its rate limits; please do not automate the web interface.
You may not use the cloud (including short links, custom domains, link-in-bio pages, booking pages, the chat widget, documents or emails sent through us) to:
ul: Phish, scam or defraud people, or collect credentials, payment details or personal data under false pretenses.
Distribute or link to malware, unwanted software, or exploits.
Send spam or unsolicited bulk messages, or use short links to hide where a link really goes.
Impersonate any person, brand or organization, or mislead people about who is behind a page or link.
Host or link to illegal content, including child sexual abuse material, content that infringes intellectual property, or content that incites violence or harassment.
Violate the privacy of others, including by publishing their personal data without a legal basis.
Attack or overload the service: probing for vulnerabilities outside our disclosure policy, scraping at abusive rates, bypassing rate limits, or trying to access other people's data.
Resell or provide access to the hosted service as if it were your own product, except as expressly allowed in a written agreement with us.

s07.h: Short links, redirects and abuse reports
p: A link shortener can be misused to disguise harmful destinations, so we treat abuse seriously. To protect people who click, we may check link destinations against our own rules and third-party reputation sources, show a warning page before redirecting, add friction such as interstitials, or disable a link, a link-in-bio page, a custom domain or an account. We may act without prior notice when there is a risk of harm; where reasonable, we will tell you what happened and why.

Short-link back-halves and link-in-bio handles are not property. We may reclaim or reassign them if they impersonate others, infringe trademarks, are reserved for the service, or have been inactive on a closed account. If you connect a custom domain, you must control it and are responsible for its DNS.
To report a malicious or abusive link, page or account, write to abuse@zerosoft.ai with the full URL and a short description. We review reports and act on them as quickly as we reasonably can.

s08.h: Your content and the data you collect
p: Your content (links, analytics, contacts, bookings, conversations, documents, files) is yours. You give us only the permission we need to host, process, transmit and display it to run the service for you and for the people you share it with. We do not use your content for advertising, we do not sell it, and we do not use it to train AI models.

Some of your content is personal data about other people: CRM contacts, booking guests, chat visitors, or people who click your links. For that data you decide what is collected and why, and you are responsible for having a legal basis for it and for telling those people how you use their data. We process it on your behalf and following your instructions, as described in our Privacy Policy.

Files you upload (for example, chat or issue attachments) are stored at hard-to-guess public URLs: anyone who has the URL can open the file. Do not upload anything that must stay strictly confidential.
You can export your data while your account is active and for 30 days after you close it. After that, we delete it as described in the Privacy Policy.

If you believe content hosted on or linked from the cloud infringes your copyright or other rights, write to abuse@zerosoft.ai with: the work you claim is infringed; the exact URL of the content; your name and contact details; a statement that you believe in good faith the use is not authorized by the rights holder or the law; a statement that the information is accurate and that you are the rights holder or authorized to act for them; and your physical or electronic signature.

We may remove or disable the content and will notify the account holder where possible. If you believe your content was removed by mistake, reply with a counter-notice explaining why; we may restore it unless the complainant shows us they have started legal action. We disable accounts of repeat infringers.

Some features connect to services we do not control: Google (sign-in, Gmail and Google Calendar when you connect them), Bitly (when you import links), your own domains and DNS provider, and the URLs you configure for webhooks. Your use of those services is governed by their own terms, and we are not responsible for them. When you send data to a webhook or third-party destination you configure, you are responsible for that destination.

Paid usage, once available, will be billed at the published prices, in arrears, without lock-in. Prices exclude taxes unless stated otherwise. We will tell you in advance, by email and on the pricing page, about any price change; the new price applies only from the next billing period after the notice period ends.

You can cancel at any time. Paid service continues until the end of the period already billed, and your data stays exportable for 30 days after closure. If an invoice remains unpaid after notice, we may limit or suspend paid features; we will not delete your account for non-payment without warning you first.
Mandatory consumer rights, such as withdrawal or refund rights that apply where you live, are not affected by this section.
You can stop using the service and close your account at any time by writing to hola@zerosoft.ai.

We may suspend or terminate your access if you seriously or repeatedly break these terms, if required by law, or if your use creates a risk to people, to the service or to us. Where possible and lawful, we will warn you first and let you export your data. If we ever discontinue the cloud as a whole, we will give at least 60 days' notice, and the open source code will still be yours to run.

We work to keep the cloud fast and available, and we post incidents and maintenance on /status. But we do not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free service, and we do not offer an uptime commitment or service-level credits on the free plan. Any service-level commitment for paid plans will be stated in writing for that plan.

To the extent permitted by law, the software is provided "as is" and the cloud "as available", without warranties of any kind, express or implied, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose and non-infringement. Keep your own copies of anything critical: export is always available.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, neither zerosoft nor its team will be liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenue, data or business, arising from the use of or inability to use the software or the cloud, even if we were advised of the possibility.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability for any claim related to the cloud is limited to the greater of the amounts you paid us for the cloud in the 12 months before the claim or USD 100.

Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability that cannot be excluded or limited by law, such as liability for fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence, or your rights as a consumer under mandatory law.

If you use the cloud for a business or organization, you agree to defend and hold zerosoft harmless from third-party claims arising from your content, your links and their destinations, the personal data you collect through the service, or your breach of these terms or of the law, to the extent permitted by law. This section does not apply to consumers where local law does not allow it.

We review these terms periodically. If we change them, we will post the new version here with its date. For material changes, we will notify account holders by email at least 15 days before they take effect. If you do not agree, you can close your account and export your data before that date; continuing to use the service after it means you accept the new terms.
Changes to these terms never change the software licenses retroactively: code you received under the AGPLv3 stays under the AGPLv3.

These terms are governed by the laws of Uruguay, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. Disputes go to the courts of Montevideo, Uruguay. If you are a consumer, you keep the protections and the forum that the mandatory law of your country gives you, for example, the Argentine Consumer Protection Law (Law 24,240) or the Brazilian Consumer Defense Code.
If any part of these terms is found unenforceable, the rest remains in effect. Not enforcing a provision is not a waiver of it.
General questions: hola@zerosoft.ai. Abuse and takedown notices: abuse@zerosoft.ai. Security: security@zerosoft.ai. Privacy: privacy@zerosoft.ai.

meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: What zerosoft.ai collects, what it never collects, and why. We collect the minimum, keep it no longer than needed, and never sell it.

privacy.label: Legal · 02
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: We collect the minimum, keep it no longer than needed, and never sell it. This policy explains exactly what that means, in the same plain language we use everywhere else. We review it periodically and whenever the product changes in a way that affects your data.

p: We need your name and email to give you an account, and a few request headers to count clicks. We do not use advertising or analytics cookies, we do not fingerprint, we do not store the IP address of people who click your links, and we do not sell or rent personal data.

This policy covers two groups of people: account holders who use zerosoft, and people who interact with what our account holders publish: people who click a short link, book a meeting, or write in a chat widget.

s02.h: Who is responsible for your data
p: zerosoft is the controller (the party that decides how and why data is used) for account data, data about the use of zerosoft.ai, and the communications we send to account holders.

For data that account holders collect through the products (CRM contacts, booking guests, chat visitors and link clicks), the account holder is the controller and zerosoft processes the data on their behalf. If you booked a meeting, chatted with a business or clicked a link and want to exercise your rights, please contact that business first; we will help them respond, and you can also write to us.
If you self-host zerosoft, you are the controller of everything in your instance and we never see it.

ul: Account data: your name, email address and profile picture, provided by Google when you sign in, plus your workspace memberships and settings.

Sign-in and security records: when you sign in we record the session (time, IP address and browser), sign-in and two-step events, and, if you turn it on, an encrypted two-step secret and hashed recovery codes. Workspace owners and admins can see these events for their members in the workspace audit log.
Workspace content: the links, contacts, deals, bookings, issues, conversations, documents and files you and your team create.

Link click data: when someone follows a short link we record the time, the link, the referrer's domain, the approximate country, the device type, the browser and the operating system. We do not store the IP address or the full user-agent string with the click.

Video view data (Rec): when someone plays a video shared from Rec we record the time, how much of the video they watched and which parts, button clicks, the name they choose to give, and, if they are signed in, their account. We also record the approximate country, region and city provided by our hosting provider, the device type, the browser, the operating system and the domain of the site they came from. We do not store the IP address or the full user-agent string with the view. Only the person who recorded the video and workspace admins who manage it can see this data.
Booking data: when someone books through a Cal page, the name, email, answers to the host's questions, time zone and language they provide, and the booking details.

Chat data: messages written in a Chat widget, the name and email if the visitor chooses to give them, attachments they upload, satisfaction ratings, and a random visitor identifier stored in the visitor's browser so the conversation continues across visits.

Google integration data, only if you connect it: for Gmail, the emails exchanged with your CRM contacts (sender, recipients, subject, date, message and thread IDs, and the message body: plain text plus a sanitized copy of the HTML, size-limited, without attachments or remote images), and the emails you send from the CRM through your Gmail; for Google Calendar, your busy and free times and the events that bookings create in your calendar.

Integration secrets: OAuth tokens for Google, and webhook signing secrets, stored encrypted. API keys are stored only as hashes. A Bitly token you give us for an import is used for that import and not stored.
Technical data: IP addresses are used briefly for rate limiting and appear in our hosting provider's request logs (see Retention). Email delivery status for the transactional emails we send.
Messages you send us: emails to our support, privacy, abuse or security addresses.

Bookings and CRM: when someone books a meeting through Cal, their name, email, the meeting time and their answers are also saved as a contact and a meeting activity in the host's CRM. When an agent chooses to, a Chat conversation is saved to the visitor's CRM contact.

Email tracking for emails sent from the CRM, when the account holder keeps it on (it can be turned off for the workspace or for each email): an invisible image and rewritten links record when the email is opened or a link is clicked: the time, the link and the browser user agent, not the IP address. Sequence emails include a link to unsubscribe; unsubscribing stops further sequence emails to that address.

Feedback: if you send feedback through the site or the app, we keep the message, the type and product you picked, the page you were on, your browser's user agent, and your email if you give it or are signed in.
No advertising or analytics cookies, and no third-party trackers on zerosoft.ai.
No device fingerprinting and no cross-site tracking.
No IP addresses stored with link clicks.
No passwords: you sign in with Google or a one-time email code. Link passwords are stored only as salted scrypt hashes.
Nothing from emails that do not involve your CRM contacts, and no attachments.
No payment card details: we do not charge today. When paid plans launch, payments will be handled by a payment processor that we will name here first.

p: We use only what is needed for the service to work: a session cookie that keeps you signed in, a language-preference cookie, a short-lived cookie that remembers you unlocked a password-protected link (up to 7 days), and browser local storage for interface preferences such as a collapsed sidebar. We also set a time-zone cookie so dates show in your local time, and a cookie with a hash of the signed-in account so pages saved for offline use are only shown to the person who saved them.

The Chat widget, when a business installs it on its website, stores a random visitor identifier in that website's local storage. It does not track the visitor on other sites. Because these are strictly necessary for features people asked for, we do not show a cookie banner; businesses that install the widget should mention it in their own privacy notice.

s06.h: How click analytics work without cookies
p: When a browser follows a short link, it tells us where it came from (the Referer header, of which we keep only the domain), what it is (the User-Agent header, which we reduce to device type, browser and operating system) and roughly where it is (a country code provided by our hosting provider at the network edge, or resolved from the IP address on self-hosted instances).
We save those few fields and never save the IP address with the click. That is enough for honest statistics (clicks per day, per referrer, per country) without following anyone around the internet.

ul: To provide the service: show your dashboard, count your clicks, schedule your bookings, deliver chat messages, sync the integrations you connect, and send the emails the products are designed to send, such as booking confirmations with calendar files.
To keep it secure: rate-limit requests, detect and stop abuse such as phishing links, block attacks, and debug errors.
To communicate with you: service and security notices, and changes to these policies. We do not send marketing emails today; if we ever do, you will be able to opt out at any time.
To comply with the law and respond to valid legal requests.
Never to sell, rent or share personal data for advertising, and never to train AI models on your content.

p: If you connect Gmail or Google Calendar, zerosoft requests only the access each feature needs: Gmail read access to show the emails exchanged with your CRM contacts in their timeline (and to detect replies that stop a sequence), Gmail send access to send the emails and sequence steps you write in the CRM from your own address, and Google Calendar free/busy plus event access to avoid double bookings and to add, update or cancel the events your bookings create. Gmail data is used only for these features: it is not used for advertising, not sold, and not used to train AI models. You can disconnect at any time from the product settings or from your Google account.
zerosoft's use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

In practice: we use Google user data only to provide and improve the user-facing features that use it; we do not transfer it to others except as needed to provide those features, to comply with the law, or as part of a merger or acquisition with notice to you; we do not use it for advertising; we do not use it to train generalized AI or machine learning models; and no human at zerosoft reads it unless you give us explicit permission for specific messages, it is necessary for security purposes such as investigating abuse, or it is required by law.

Under the GDPR (EEA and UK) and Brazil's LGPD, we process account data and workspace content to perform our contract with you; security data, rate limiting, logs and abuse prevention under our legitimate interest in running a safe, reliable service (and to prevent fraud); and data needed to meet legal obligations under those obligations. Where we rely on consent, such as optional integrations, you can withdraw it at any time by disconnecting them.

Under Argentina's Personal Data Protection Law (Law 25,326), we process data with your consent or because it is necessary for the contractual relationship with you, within the exceptions the law provides.

We do not sell personal data. We share it only with the service providers (subprocessors) that run the cloud for us, under contractual confidentiality and data-protection terms, and only as needed for their job: The current list, with what each provider processes, is on our subprocessors page (/subprocessors).
ul: Vercel: hosting, serverless functions, file storage for uploads (Vercel Blob), scheduled jobs and the AI Gateway.
Turso: the database where account and workspace data is stored.
Railway: runs the WhatsApp gateway used by Lines and Inbox when you connect a WhatsApp number.
Resend: delivery of transactional emails, such as sign-in codes, workspace invitations, notifications and booking confirmations.
Google: sign-in, and Gmail and Google Calendar only when you connect them.
AI model providers, through the Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter, only for AI features you use, under terms that do not allow training on your content.
Destinations you choose: if you configure webhooks or the API, data is sent to the URLs and tools you set up.
Authorities, when the law genuinely requires it; we will push back on requests that are overly broad.
A successor, if zerosoft is merged or acquired; we will notify you before your data becomes subject to a different privacy policy.

p: Our providers process data in the United States and possibly other countries, which may not offer the same level of protection as yours. Where the GDPR, the LGPD or Law 25,326 require it, we rely on appropriate safeguards for these transfers, such as standard contractual clauses offered by our providers. If we change providers or the region where data is stored, we will update this page in advance.

ul: Account data and workspace content: kept while your account is active.

After you close your account: exportable for 30 days, then deleted from the production database. Remaining copies in provider backups expire on the providers' backup schedules, and we aim for full deletion within 90 days.
Link click data: kept as individual records without IP addresses while the link and account exist, so you can see your history.
Video view data (Rec): kept without IP addresses while the video exists. Deleting the video deletes its views.
Rate-limit records: they contain the IP address and are deleted automatically shortly after their window ends (at most 10 minutes).
Sessions and the security audit log (IP address and browser): sessions are deleted 90 days after they end; audit log entries after one year.
Hosting request logs: they include IP addresses and are kept by our hosting provider for a limited period under its retention settings; we do not copy them into long-term storage.
Booking, chat and CRM data: kept as long as the account holder keeps it, or until they or you request deletion.
We may keep limited data longer when the law requires it or to resolve disputes and prevent abuse, for example records of accounts suspended for phishing.

p: We protect data with HTTPS, encryption of secrets at rest, hashing of keys and passwords, and least-privilege access. Details are on our Security page. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affects your personal data, we will notify you and the competent authorities as the applicable law requires.

Wherever you live, you can ask us to access, correct, delete or export your personal data, to restrict or object to its processing, and to withdraw consent. Depending on your country you may have additional rights, such as confirmation that we process your data and information about who we share it with (LGPD), or free access to your data at intervals of at least six months (Law 25,326).

You can download all your data as a ZIP and delete your account or workspace yourself in Settings › Profile, and each app has its own export. For anything else, write to privacy@zerosoft.ai. We may need to verify your identity. We answer within the deadline set by your local law (for example, 10 calendar days for access requests under Argentine law) and in any case within 30 days.
Businesses that need a data processing agreement (GDPR art. 28) can request ours at privacy@zerosoft.ai.

You also have the right to complain to a data protection authority: in the EEA or UK, your local supervisory authority; in Brazil, the ANPD; in Argentina, the Agency for Access to Public Information (AAIP), which, as the enforcement body of Law 25,326, is empowered to handle complaints from anyone whose rights are affected by non-compliance with data protection rules. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.

Accounts are for adults. The service is not directed at children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you believe a child has given us personal data, write to privacy@zerosoft.ai and we will delete it.

If you run zerosoft on your own servers, your data stays wherever you put it and this policy does not apply to it. We receive nothing from your instance: license keys for enterprise features are verified offline.
We review this policy periodically. Changes will be posted here with a new date; material changes will be announced to account holders by email at least 15 days before they take effect.
Privacy questions, requests and complaints: privacy@zerosoft.ai.

meta.title: Security
meta.description: How zerosoft protects the service: two-step verification, server-side sessions, audit log, field-level encryption with key rotation, scanning in CI, data export and deletion, and our honest compliance status.

security.label: Legal · 03
security.title: Security
security.intro: Trust is earned with specifics, not badges. Here is exactly how we protect the service today, what we do not claim, and how to tell us when we got something wrong. We review this page periodically and whenever these controls change.

p: Minimal data, two-step verification, sessions you can see and revoke, an audit log for every workspace, secrets encrypted with rotating keys, and a codebase anyone can read.

Compliance status, plainly: zerosoft does not hold a SOC 2 report or an ISO 27001 certificate, and no independent audit or penetration test has been performed yet. Our controls are designed to meet the SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, and the policies and control matrix are public in our repository (docs/security). When an audit starts or finishes, this page will say so.
There are no zerosoft passwords. You sign in with Google (verified email addresses only) or with a one-time code sent to your email.

You can turn on two-step verification with any authenticator app (TOTP), with ten single-use recovery codes. Workspace owners can require it for every member: someone without it cannot open that workspace until they turn it on.

Every sign-in is a session on our side. In Settings › Security you see your devices, when each was last active, and you can sign out one or all of them; signing out ends that session on the server too. Sessions expire after 30 days without use.
Each workspace has owners, admins, members and guests, access per app and per record. Every page and API checks these rules on the server.

Owners and admins see a security audit log: sign-ins, two-step changes, sessions closed, API keys created or revoked, exports, deletions and member changes, with time and IP. It can be downloaded as CSV and is kept for one year.

Programmatic access uses API keys with the zs_ prefix. Keys are generated from a cryptographically secure random source, shown to you exactly once, stored only as SHA-256 hashes, scoped to the apps you choose, and revocable instantly. A member's keys stop working when they leave the workspace.
Each key is rate-limited to 100 requests per minute.

Password-protected short links store their passwords as scrypt hashes with a random salt per link. Once a visitor unlocks a link, a signed cookie remembers it for up to 7 days, and attempts are rate-limited per IP and per link.
In transit: all traffic uses HTTPS with modern TLS, plain HTTP is redirected, and browsers are told to use HTTPS only (HSTS). Connections to our database and to our own services also use TLS.

At rest: our infrastructure providers encrypt stored data and backups. On top of that we encrypt secrets ourselves before they reach the database (OAuth tokens, third-party API keys, webhook secrets, connected-account settings, credentials and two-step secrets) with AES-256-GCM, a separate key for every value, and master keys that we can rotate. Private files such as CVs and signed PDFs are encrypted before upload.

End to end: locked notes are encrypted in your browser and we cannot read them. We do not encrypt everything end to end, because search, AI features, integrations, automations and real-time collaboration need the server to read the content. No security standard requires it; we use it where the server does not need to read the data.

Files attached in the apps are stored at URLs with long random names. They are hard to guess but not private: anyone with the URL can open the file. File types that browsers would execute (HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript) are rejected. Private files (CVs, signed documents, receipts) never get a public URL.
Click analytics are cookie-less and fingerprint-less: referrer domain, country and device are derived from request headers, and the IP address is never stored with the click.

IP addresses are used briefly for rate limiting and are recorded with sign-ins and sessions so you can recognize your devices; those records are deleted after one year (audit log) and 90 days after a session ends.

Public endpoints, sign-in codes and two-step codes are rate-limited. Outgoing requests to URLs you configure, such as webhooks, are restricted to public internet hosts with timeouts. We may disable short links used for phishing, malware or spam; report abuse to abuse@zerosoft.ai.

Every change goes through a pull request and automated checks before it ships: type checks, unit and end-to-end tests, a production build, static analysis with CodeQL, secret scanning and a dependency audit. Dependabot watches our dependencies, and security-relevant changes get an independent review.

The cloud runs on Vercel (hosting, functions, files), Turso (database) and Railway (WhatsApp gateway), sends email with Resend, and uses AI model providers only for AI features you use. The full list, with what each one processes, is on the subprocessors page (/subprocessors). Their certifications are theirs, not ours. Access to production is limited to the people who need it and protected with two-step verification.

In Settings › Profile you can download everything in your account and workspace as a ZIP, and delete your account or your workspace. Deletion happens 30 days after you ask (you can cancel until then) and covers database records, uploaded files and connected WhatsApp numbers; copies in provider backups expire within their retention window.
Customers who need a data processing agreement can request ours at privacy@zerosoft.ai.

The code of the products is public. You do not have to trust this page: you can read the code, run it yourself and check every claim. Reports from people who do exactly that are our favorite kind of email.

Email security@zerosoft.ai with a description, steps to reproduce and the impact. Please do not open public issues for security problems. We aim to acknowledge within 72 hours, keep you updated, and credit you when the fix ships if you want. We do not run a paid bug bounty.

Test only against your own accounts and data, do not degrade the service, send spam or use social engineering, and give us a reasonable window before publishing. If you act in good faith, we will not pursue legal action against you.

If we learn of a security incident that affects your data, we investigate and contain it, notify affected account holders without undue delay so they can meet their own 72-hour duties, and notify data protection authorities when the law requires it. Service incidents are posted on /status.

meta.title: Subprocessors
meta.description: The service providers that process personal data for zerosoft cloud, what each one does and where.

subprocessors.label: Legal · 04
subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.intro: These are the companies that process personal data on behalf of zerosoft cloud customers. We announce changes here at least 15 days before a new subprocessor starts processing personal data. Self-hosted instances use none of them unless their operator configures them.

ul: Vercel Inc. (United States): hosting, serverless functions, scheduled jobs, file storage (Vercel Blob), request logs and the AI Gateway. Processes all data in transit, uploaded files and request logs with IP addresses.
Turso / ChiselStrike Inc.: the database and its backups. Stores account and workspace data.
Railway Corp. (United States): runs the WhatsApp gateway used by Lines and Inbox. Processes messages, contacts and media of connected WhatsApp numbers.
Resend Inc. (United States): delivers transactional and service emails. Processes recipient addresses, email content and delivery events.

s02.h: Used only when you use the feature
ul: Google LLC (United States): sign in with Google, and Gmail and Google Calendar when you connect them.

AI model providers, reached through the Vercel AI Gateway (Anthropic by default) or OpenRouter Inc. (United States): AI features such as the assistant, agents, summaries and drafting. They receive the prompt and the content you send to that feature, under terms that do not allow training on it.

p: Integrations you connect with your own account (Slack, Microsoft 365, Stripe, Twilio, Meta, GitHub, Notion, webhooks, the API and MCP clients) receive data because you tell them to, under your own agreement with that provider.

Where data leaves the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, we rely on the Standard Contractual Clauses and, where certified, the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, as set out in each provider's data processing terms. Customers can request our data processing agreement at privacy@zerosoft.ai, and can subscribe to changes to this list there.
